entry.name: STAG
entry.title: Learning the signatures of the human grasp using a scalable tactile glove
entry.summary: Knitted glove with 548 piezoresistive sensors over the palmar side of the right hand, read as a 32x32 grid at ~7.3 Hz; one subject grasping 26 objects, plus blindfolded, weight and hand-pose sets with synchronized RGB frames.
entry.hand: human right hand wearing the STAG knitted tactile glove

sensor.note: One sample = a 32x32 int16 map of raw 10-bit ADC counts (0-1023 = 0-5 V amplifier output) from the 32 row x 32 column conductive-thread electrodes; 548 cells are physical sensors, the other 476 are constant. Rest ~510-516, useful signal 500-650, readings over 950 are shorted electrodes. Normal force only.
sensor.range: 30 mN-0.5 N working range per element (responds from ~25 mN, saturates beyond 0.8 N); ~150 quantization levels, ~17.5% peak hysteresis

scale.text: ~6.9 h, 221 recordings, 177,592 tactile frames (135,187 object interaction + 6,686 blindfolded + 11,682 weights + 24,037 hand poses), 26 objects, 1 subject, right hand

entry.access: Open download (no login) of four zip archives from stag.csail.mit.edu/datasets/, each also as a pressure-only 'lite' zip (49 MB in total).
entry.license: STAG Research License (research use only, non-commercial, no redistribution)
caveats: License forbids copying or distributing the data other than for your own backup.
Grasping, object identification, weighing and hand-pose articulation, not task-level manipulation.
All recordings are from one person (an author) wearing the glove on the right hand.
Tactile values are raw ADC counts, not calibrated force; the release has no force calibration.
No hand or object tracking; hand-pose classes G1-G7 are labels of articulated poses.
Tactile maps are stored on the 32x32 electrode grid; the sensor-to-hand layout is only embedded in the project's demo pages (sensorIndices/sensorLayout), not in the dataset files.
Camera images were recorded for illustration only and are not used by the authors' code.

other: per-frame preprocessing flags (valid label, balanced, grasp, transition) and train/test split

unconfirmed: hours = 6.9: sum over the 221 recordings of (last ts - first ts) in the four lite metadata.mat files: classification 5.28 h, blindfolded 0.26 h, weights 0.45 h, hand poses 0.92 h. The paper says recordings exceed 5 hours (object set).

episodes = 221 recordings counted in the metadata.mat files: classification 82 (26 objects x 3 days + 4 empty-hand, batches 000/001/002 with 27/27/28), blindfolded 105 (104 identification attempts + 1 empty-hand control), weights 27 (26 objects + empty hand, ~60 s each), hand poses 7 sessions (~452-480 s each, several pose classes per recording).
frames = 177,592: 135,187 + 6,686 + 11,682 + 24,037 frames in the four metadata.mat files; the first and last two match the paper.
tasks = 4 counts the recording protocols (visually aware object interaction, blindfolded identification, weight lift-hold-drop, hand-pose articulation); the paper does not define tasks.
rate_hz = 7.3 is the paper's average frame rate; ts in the files gives a median interval of 0.136 s (7.35 Hz) and a mean of 7.12-7.28 Hz per subset (intervals up to ~0.176 s at p95).

Camera resolution 682x512 is that of the released JPEG frames (fetched from all four archives); the native camera resolution and the camera mount are not stated. The frames show a close view of the gloved hand over a table.

548 valid sensors: exactly 548 of the 1024 grid cells vary in every subset; the other cells are constant 510. The demo page's sensorIndices (32x32, 548 non-negative) matches this mask exactly and sensorLayout gives 2-D hand coordinates per sensor.
Classification values span 446-1000; 51 frames contain a reading above 950 (the paper's shorted-electrode criterion).
scenes not stated; all recordings appear to be on one table surface (from the camera frames).

download.format: Four zip archives (classification, blindfolded, weights, handposes), stored uncompressed. Each holds metadata.mat (MATLAB v5, all frames of the subset with labels) and <batch>/<recording>/{000000..N.jpg, viz/000000..N.jpg, pressuredata.mat}. Lite zips hold only metadata.mat + readme.
download.total_size: 19.15 GB full (classification 14,692,607,623 B; blindfolded 433,316,009 B; weights 1,147,984,210 B; handposes 2,876,309,121 B); lite 48,971,024 B (38.4 MB + 1.7 MB + 3.0 MB + 5.9 MB)
download.per_episode: Pressure of every recording is in the lite metadata.mat (39 MB for all 82 object recordings). With video: one classification recording ~1,357 frames x (73 KB jpg + 32 KB viz) + ~3.4 MB pressuredata.mat, about 140 MB.
download.partial_fetch: Server accepts HTTP range requests and the zips are stored (no compression), so single members (one recording's JPEGs or pressuredata.mat) can be read after fetching the central directory from the zip64 end record.

channels.name: metadata.mat:pressure
channels.shape: (N, 32, 32) int16, N = all frames of the subset
channels.unit: raw 10-bit ADC counts (0-1023 = 0-5 V amplifier output), not calibrated force
channels.frame: 32x32 grid of row x column conductive-thread electrodes on the right-hand glove (palmar side); 548 cells are sensors, 476 are constant 510. Sensor -> hand position only in the demo pages (sensorIndices, sensorLayout)
channels.note: Normal force per sensor. Rest ~510-516; useful 500-650 (paper normalizes 500-650 to 0-1); >950 = shorted electrode. Observed ranges: classification 446-1000, blindfolded 509-991, weights 510-654, hand poses 510-992.

channels.name: <batch>/<recording>/pressuredata.mat:data
channels.shape: (N, 32, 32) int16, N = frames in the recording
channels.note: Per-recording raw pressure, same values as metadata.mat; only in the full zips. Checked on blindfolded/000/005-mug (32 frames, 510-562).

channels.name: <batch>/<recording>/pressuredata.mat:tStamp / frame
channels.unit: Unix time in s / frame index
channels.note: Absolute capture timestamps (e.g. 2019-01-12 for the blindfolded set) and zero-based frame numbers matching the JPEG names.

channels.name: metadata.mat:ts / frame / batchId / recordingId
channels.unit: s since the recording's first frame / index
channels.note: Per-frame time and indices into batches/recordings; frame selects <batch>/<recording>/<frame:06d>.jpg.

channels.name: <batch>/<recording>/<frame>.jpg
channels.frame: third-person view of the gloved hand (FLIR GS2-GE-20S4C-C), mount not stated
channels.note: Recorded 'for illustration', one image per tactile frame (135,191 JPEGs for 135,187 frames in classification). Only in the full zips.

channels.name: <batch>/<recording>/viz/<frame>.jpg
channels.frame: side-by-side: downsized camera image + 32x32 pressure map without spatial layout
channels.note: Pressure mapped from 500-650 to 0-1 in log space; bar below is green when hasValidLabel. Only in the full zips.

channels.name: metadata.mat:objects / objectId
channels.note: 26 objects + empty_hand; in handposes the classes are empty_hand, G1-G7 and several classes occur in one recording.

channels.name: metadata.mat:weights (weights subset) and weights/000/weights.xlsx
channels.note: Ground-truth object weight, 0 (empty hand) to 679 (cat sculpture).

channels.name: metadata.mat:graspIndex / graspValid (weights subset)
channels.note: Index of the 10 s grasp interval in the 1 min recording (0-6); graspValid marks the 4-6 s hold window used by the paper.

channels.name: metadata.mat:splits / splitId / hasValidLabel / isBalanced / isGrasp / isTransition / transitionDir
channels.note: Paper preprocessing: train/test split, object-held flag (88,269 frames in classification), balanced subset, reliable contact, last empty frame before contact. transitionDir (int32 0-74) is in the file but not documented; the readme names 'isGrap' while the file has isGrasp.

channels.name: metadata.mat:actionStartTS / actionEndTS (blindfolded subset)
channels.note: Start of unaware manipulation and moment the object was identified.

episode_index.where: metadata.mat in each lite or full zip: recordings (names '<nnn>-<object>'), batches, and per-frame recordingId/batchId/objectId/ts; full-zip directory listing <subset>/<batch>/<recording>/
tasks: visually aware object interaction (classification, 3-5 min per object, 3 days)
weight estimation: grasp from above, lift, hold, drop every 10 s for 1 min
hand-pose articulation: empty hand and G1-G7 from a grasp taxonomy

sample.reason: The STAG Research License forbids redistribution: "The Licensed Material will not be copied nor distributed in any form other than for Your backup." (http://stag.csail.mit.edu/license.html, identical in https://github.com/Erkil1452/touch/blob/master/LICENSE). Licensed Material covers the data, models and related source, so no sample is re-hosted. The data itself is open (no login) and would otherwise qualify; candidates for a sample if permission is granted are listed under candidates_if_permitted.
sample.fetch_estimate: 0 (nothing fetched for the sample). If permitted: ~160 MB by range requests (JPEG + viz frames of the four windows, ~105 KB per frame x ~1,440 frames, plus four pressuredata.mat of ~3.4 MB); pressure alone is already in the 49 MB lite zips.
sample.rules_applied: README step 2: license explicitly forbids redistribution -> skip_forbidden, row added to SKIPPED.md. Candidates follow the 'how many' rules anyway (4 protocols <= 6 -> all; one episode each, 4 total; 10-60 s windows holding contact), checked only against the already-downloaded lite metadata.mat (all 548 sensor cells present, no shorted cells >950 in these recordings, max(sensor) > 540 counts for >= 5 s).
